name: Receive and set up credit applications
summary: Every credit application, whether keyed by the vendor desk, submitted by a dealer or account executive in the portal or emailed by a broker, is set up by a credit coordinator before an analyst sees it. The coordinator checks it is complete and consented, looks for duplicates and existing exposure, verifies the business in the corporate registry, pulls commercial reports from Equifax and PayNet and personal reports on the guarantors, screens names and clears fraud flags, then routes the file to small-ticket or mid-ticket credit or to fraud review. Missing signatures and statements are the most common delay, and pulling bureau reports through separate portals means typing the same data several times.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor with a nine-person credit support team setting up about 3,400 applications a month from vendor, broker and direct channels.
baseline.notes: Origination portal with an Equifax consumer link, separate Equifax commercial and PayNet web logins, rule-based fraud flags in the decision engine; broker applications still often arrived by email.

trigger: A credit application is submitted in the origination portal or arrives by email at the broker desk.
end_state: The file is set up, bureau reports are attached and it sits in the small-ticket or mid-ticket adjudication queue, or it has been referred to fraud review, closed as a duplicate or withdrawn for missing information.

volume.seasonality: Follows equipment sales: busier in spring and early autumn and at month ends, about 15% lower in the second quarter of 2020.

evidence.note: From the organisation's demand driver for applications received across all channels (about 1,850 vendor, 1,100 broker and 480 direct a month).
Duties and salary from the posting; organisation file cost (salary loaded x1.35 and scaled to 2019-2022). About 8.5 of the 9 coordinators' time; the rest is fraud back-up and vendor approvals.
The posting describes a manager running quality assurance audits; the share of time is a tier C estimate.
Broker desk inbox monitoring is described; about a third of four coordinators' time goes to keying emailed broker applications and relaying requests (tier C share).
Vendor desk coordinators relay credit's missing-item requests to dealers; a small share of the desk's time.

systems.name: Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Commercial and consumer credit bureau portals (Equifax, PayNet)
Rule-based credit scoring and decision engine
Customer relationship management system (partner accounts, pipeline, commissions data)
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Federal and provincial corporate registry searches (web and search-provider portals)

steps.name: Application arrives for credit
steps.description: A credit application reaches credit support either as a file submitted in the origination portal by the vendor desk, a dealer, an account executive or lease administration, or as an email package from a broker to the broker desk inbox. The portal stamps the time and places portal files in the intake queue.
outputs: intake queue item or broker email

evidence.note: Portal and email submission routes are described; the 24% email share is a tier C estimate.

steps.name: Triage broker email submission
steps.description: A broker desk coordinator opens the next email in the broker desk mailbox, checks in the CRM that the broker is on the approved panel and in good standing, saves the application, owner consent and any financial statements to a new file and replies with an acknowledgement.

error.defect_description: Attachment from one broker email saved to another file.

control.basis: Broker program agreement: applications accepted only from approved brokers on the panel

evidence.note: Monitoring and routing of emails to the broker desk is described; times are tier C.

steps.name: Key broker application into portal
steps.description: The broker desk coordinator re-types the broker's application from the PDF into the portal: legal and operating names, address, business number, years in business, owners and their addresses and dates of birth, equipment, cost, term and structure, and attaches the images so the file joins the intake queue.

error.defect_description: Typing error in a name, address or date of birth that later causes a bureau no-hit or mismatch.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; re-keying a two-page application.

steps.name: Check application completeness
steps.description: A credit coordinator opens the next file in the intake queue and checks that the application is complete and legible: legal name, address, owners, equipment, cost and structure, a signed consent page for each owner, a supplier quote or invoice and, for deals over $250,000, two years of financial statements with interims.
outputs: complete file or list of gaps

error.defect_description: A missing item is not noticed and the analyst has to ask for it later.

control.basis: Credit policy minimum application requirements by deal size

evidence.note: Application set-up and the financial statement requirement above $250,000 are documented; the 22% incomplete share is tier C.

steps.name: Log gaps and notify originator
steps.description: The coordinator lists the missing items in the portal file, puts it on hold and emails or posts a portal message to whoever submitted it: the vendor desk for dealer files, the broker desk for broker files or the account executive for direct deals.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; a short hold note.

steps.name: Vendor desk relays request to dealer
steps.description: A vendor desk coordinator picks up the hold notice, phones or emails the dealer with the list of missing items and explains what the customer must sign or provide, then watches for the reply.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; relayed by phone or email.

steps.name: Broker desk relays request to broker
steps.description: A broker desk coordinator emails the broker the list of missing items, often an owner's signature, financial statements or a supplier invoice, and notes the request in the broker's file.

evidence.note: The posting names responding to broker requests as a coordinator duty; times are tier C.

steps.name: Originator and customer supply missing items
steps.description: The dealer, broker or account executive goes back to the customer for the missing signature, details or statements and sends them in. Statements and signatures from owners on job sites often take a day or more, and some customers drop the application.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; two hours to three days.

steps.name: Check for duplicate open applications
steps.description: The coordinator searches the portal for open or recent applications for the same customer, owners or equipment, because brokers and dealers sometimes submit the same deal through more than one channel.

error.defect_description: Duplicate missed because of a spelling difference.

control.basis: Channel conflict rule in the dealer and broker program agreements: first complete submission keeps the deal

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; a name and phone search.

steps.name: Supervisor resolves duplicate submission
steps.description: The credit support supervisor compares the files, decides which channel submitted first and whether they are the same deal, informs the originating desks and closes or merges the later file.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; needs a call with the sales desks.

steps.name: Match customer to existing accounts and exposure
steps.description: The coordinator searches the lease management system by legal name, phone number and each guarantor for existing contracts, adds up current exposure across related companies, notes payment history and any open collection or deferral, and links the application to the customer record.

error.defect_description: Related company exposure missed, which can send a file to the wrong authority level.

next.condition: new customer or registration not verified in the last year
existing customer verified within the last year

evidence.note: Gathering internal and third-party data at set-up is described; the 25% repeat share is tier C.

steps.name: Verify business registration
steps.description: The coordinator searches the federal or provincial corporate registry for the legal name to confirm the business exists and is active, its incorporation date for time in business and its directors, and compares them with the application. Sole proprietors are checked against business name registrations.

error.defect_description: Wrong entity with a similar name accepted as the applicant.

control.basis: Credit policy customer identification: confirm the legal existence and status of the applicant; securitisation funders accept only verified legal entities

evidence.note: Corporate registry searches at set-up are described; times are tier C.

steps.name: Pull commercial bureau reports
steps.description: The coordinator logs in to the Equifax commercial portal and the PayNet portal separately, re-enters the business name, address and phone in each, picks the closest matching entity and saves both reports, noting payment index, delinquency and failure scores, legal items and lease payment history.

error.defect_description: Report pulled on the wrong entity among similar names.

evidence.note: Equifax and PayNet pulls through separate log-ins with repeated data entry are documented; times are tier C.

steps.name: Pull personal bureau reports on guarantors
steps.description: For each owner who will guarantee, the coordinator confirms a signed consent is on file, then requests the Equifax consumer report through the portal's bureau link and attaches it. Most small-ticket files have one or two guarantors.

error.defect_description: Report pulled for the wrong person with a similar name.

control.basis: PIPEDA Schedule 1 Principle 4.3: personal credit report pulled only with the guarantor's signed consent on file, one consent per hard inquiry

next.condition: no hit, thin file or identity mismatch

evidence.note: Consent before hard inquiries and personal checks on small business owners are documented; the 10% exception share is tier C.

steps.name: Resolve bureau no-hit or mismatch
steps.description: When a bureau returns no file, several possible matches or an address or birth date that does not agree, the coordinator checks the keyed data against the application image, re-runs the search with previous addresses or alternate names and, if needed, asks the originator to confirm details.

next.condition: originator must confirm or correct details

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; keying errors upstream cause many of these.

steps.name: Screen names against sanctions lists
steps.description: The coordinator runs the business, its directors and guarantors through the sanctions screening tool or the consolidated Canadian and US lists and records the result. A possible match is passed to the fraud analyst for review.
inputs: names of business, directors and guarantors

control.basis: Special Economic Measures Act and related regulations prohibit dealing with designated persons; screening itself is company policy and a securitisation funder requirement, since non-bank lessors had no AML obligation before April 2025

evidence.note: The legal basis is documented; how independents screened in 2019-2022 is a tier C estimate.

steps.name: Run fraud and identity rules
steps.description: The decision engine runs the lessor's fraud rules over the keyed data and bureau results: bureau fraud alerts, residential or mail-drop business addresses, a business registered only weeks ago, phone and address mismatches, owners on several recent applications and dealers not on the approved list.

control.basis: Fraud prevention policy: automated red-flag rules on every new application

evidence.note: Rule-based pre-screen edits in lease origination software are documented; the flag rate is tier C.

steps.name: Review fraud and identity flags
steps.description: The coordinator looks at each flag against the documents and registry results, for example confirming that a home-based business is plausible for the industry, and either clears the flag with a note or refers the file to the fraud analyst.

error.defect_description: A real red flag is cleared as a false positive.

control.basis: Fraud prevention policy: flags cleared only with a documented reason

evidence.note: Coordinators flag unusual findings for analysts per the posting; the clear rate is tier C.

steps.name: Refer file to fraud analyst
steps.description: The coordinator writes a referral note in the portal listing the flags and what was checked, places a fraud hold so the file cannot be decided, and assigns it to the fraud analyst queue. The credit decision waits for the analyst's clearance.

evidence.note: Tier C estimate from the author's knowledge of lessor credit operations; a referral note and hold.

steps.name: Decide routing
steps.description: The coordinator decides where the file goes: small-ticket credit when the amount and the customer's total exposure stay at or below $250,000, mid-ticket credit above that, and a senior analyst flag for existing customers with arrears or for restricted equipment. Hot vendor deals are marked for priority.

error.defect_description: File routed to small-ticket although related exposure exceeds $250,000.

control.basis: Credit policy delegated authority by deal size and total exposure

evidence.note: An application-only track up to $250,000 and a fuller track above it are documented; the routing rules are tier C.

steps.name: Write set-up notes and preliminary package
steps.description: The coordinator writes a short set-up summary in the portal: registry result, bureau highlights for the business and each guarantor, existing exposure and payment history, flags cleared and anything unusual, so the analyst can start without re-reading every report.

error.defect_description: A derogatory item such as a judgment is left out of the summary.

next.condition: picked for the supervisor's quality sample

evidence.note: Assembling preliminary credit packages is a posted duty; times are tier C.

steps.name: Supervisor checks a sample of set-ups
steps.description: The credit support supervisor re-checks a sample of completed set-ups against the bureau reports and registry results for accuracy and consent, records findings for coaching and asks the coordinator to correct any error in the file.

control.basis: Credit support quality assurance and compliance audit program

evidence.note: Quality assurance and compliance audits are described in the posting; the 4% sample is tier C.

steps.name: Route file to credit queue
steps.description: The portal moves the file to the small-ticket queue, where the decision engine scores it, or to the mid-ticket underwriting queue, and updates the status the originator sees.
outputs: credit application in the adjudication queue

evidence.note: Automatic routing to queues is documented; the 87/13 split follows the organisation file's assumption that 87% of applications are $250,000 or less.

exceptions.name: Incomplete application
exceptions.description: A signature, owner detail, supplier invoice or required financial statements are missing; the file goes on hold while the originating desk chases the customer, and about 15% of these are withdrawn.

exceptions.name: Bureau no-hit or identity mismatch
exceptions.description: A bureau returns no file or a mismatch, often because of a keying error upstream; the coordinator re-searches and sometimes has to ask the originator to confirm details.

exceptions.name: Fraud flag referred
exceptions.description: Flags that the coordinator cannot clear, and possible sanctions matches, go to the fraud analyst with a hold on the file.

exceptions.name: Duplicate submission
exceptions.description: The same deal arrives through two channels and the supervisor decides which file survives.

exceptions.name: Emailed broker application
exceptions.description: Broker packages arrive by email and are re-keyed by the broker desk before set-up.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from submission to file in an adjudication queue or referred
benchmarks.population: Credit support at Canadian independent small-ticket lessors, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Same-day set-up is the norm because small-ticket lessors promise decisions within hours (Marlin's analysts are usually ready to decide within two hours of receipt); files waiting for missing items take one to three days. No published figure for set-up alone was found.
Covers set-up and analysis together, so intake must take well under two hours for typical files.

benchmarks.population: Equifax claim for Canadian asset-based lenders combining Equifax commercial and PayNet data (2024)

evidence.note: Vendor claim; implies separate pulls in 2019-2022 took about twice the effort.
3,430 applications over about 21 working days shared by about 8.5 coordinator FTE.

pain_points.description: Incomplete applications are the main delay: files sit on hold while the vendor or broker desk chases a signature or statements, and the originator often has to go back to the customer twice.

evidence.note: The organisation file names missing information as the most common delay.

pain_points.description: Commercial reports come from two bureaus with separate log-ins, so the coordinator re-types the business details in each portal and reconciles different entity matches by hand.

evidence.note: Multiple log-ins, repeated entry and manual reconciliation are described.

pain_points.description: Broker applications arrive as email PDFs and are re-keyed, and keying errors surface later as bureau no-hits that need rework.

evidence.note: Email submissions to the broker desk are described; the error link is tier C.

pain_points.description: Files submitted late in the day or overnight wait until the next morning, while dealers expect an answer within hours.

evidence.note: Competitors advertise decisions within two hours; queue waits are tier C.

sources.title: Credit Coordinator, Bennington Financial (job posting)
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor's credit coordinator monitors and routes emails and online applications to the broker desk, sets up new credit applications, gathers third-party data (land and corporate registries), pulls Equifax and PayNet reports, flags unusual findings for the credit analyst, assembles preliminary credit packages and assists the manager with quality assurance audits; salary $42,000 to $46,000.

sources.title: Equifax Business Credit Report user guide
sources.supports: The Canadian commercial report returns the legal entity that most closely matches the inquiry, a Payment Index from 0 to 99 based on the last 90 days, a Commercial Delinquency Score from 101 to 662, a Business Failure Risk Score from 1001 to 1722, trade, collection, legal and inquiry details.

sources.title: Business Gateway: an all-in-one credit performance solution for asset-based lenders
sources.supports: Before a combined product, asset-based lenders checked Equifax commercial and PayNet leasing data through multiple log-ins and reports, entered credentials and information several times and reconciled fragmented results manually; the combined report claims at least twice the speed.

sources.title: Equifax acquires PayNet
sources.supports: In April 2019 Equifax acquired PayNet, which supplies commercial leasing payment data and credit risk tools to commercial finance and leasing companies in the US and Canada.

sources.title: PIPEDA Report of Findings #2015-005: dealer ran credit checks without consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Under PIPEDA Principle 4.3 an organisation should obtain separate consent for each hard credit inquiry and retain proof of consent.

sources.title: PIPEDA case summary 2003-117: bank requires credit check on small business account applicant
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: A personal credit check on the owner of a small business is a legitimate requirement where credit risk is involved, with consent.

sources.title: Canadian sanctions: frequently asked questions
sources.supports: Canadian sanctions must be respected by any person in Canada; a dealings ban prohibits persons in Canada from dealing with designated persons; the consolidated list is a screening aid without force of law.

sources.title: Anti-money laundering obligations for factors, cheque cashers and financing/leasing entities
sources.supports: Financing and leasing entities became reporting entities under the PCMLTFA only as of April 1, 2025.

sources.title: Oracle Financial Services Lending and Leasing: Lease Origination User Guide, Underwriting
sources.supports: Lease origination software runs pre-screen edits when an application is entered, pulls the bureau report, scores the application and routes it to an auto-approve, auto-reject or underwriting queue; stagnant applications are aged into a separate queue.

sources.title: Marlin Business Services Corp. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019
sources.supports: Applications arrive by fax, phone, internet, mail, e-mail and web portal; within two hours of receipt the analyst is usually ready to decide deals under $50,000; when information is insufficient the analyst requests more.

sources.title: Equipment leasing over $250,000
sources.supports: Above $250,000 a lessor asks for two years of financial statements plus interim statements, tax returns and a list of current loans and leases; up to $250,000 is application-only.

sources.title: Search for a federal corporation
sources.publisher: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
sources.supports: Federal corporations can be searched by name, corporation number or business number and filtered by status; provincial corporations are searched in the provincial registries.

assumptions: Shares of arriving applications follow the organisation file's channel drivers: about 26% keyed by the vendor desk, 27% submitted by dealers in the portal, 32% from brokers, 14% from direct account executives and about 1% lease assumptions. The credit bureau link (bureau reports coming back) does not start cases, so its share is 0.
About 24% of applications, mostly from brokers, still arrived by email and were re-keyed by the broker desk.

Non-bank lessors had no anti-money laundering identification duty before April 1, 2025; registry checks, sanctions screening and fraud rules are company policy driven by credit risk, fraud losses and securitisation funders.
Corporate registry searches are not a system in the organisation file; a corporate_registry_search system was added here.
Routing uses total exposure including related companies: about 87% of files go to small-ticket credit, matching the organisation file's assumption.
The sanctions screening step is modelled for every file; a share of 2019-2022 independents screened only at funding.

Staffing: about 8.5 of the 9 credit coordinators' time is on intake, slightly below the hands-on time the model implies; the organisation file's nine coordinators look tight for 3,430 applications a month and some set-up is likely absorbed by analysts or overtime.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
